test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said to me, "Where have you been all this while?"

options.text: He asked me where had I been all that while.
He asked me where I have been all that while.
He asked me where I had been all that while.
He asked where I was being all this while.

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. He asked me where I had been all that while.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech, and the task is to convert it into indirect speech.
 
• When converting a question in direct speech into indirect speech:
 
 
• The reporting verb "said to" changes to "asked."
 
• The question structure changes into a statement structure.
 
• The tense of the verb in the question is adjusted according to the rules of reported speech.
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in the present perfect tense ("Where have you been"). When converted into indirect speech, the verb shifts to the past perfect tense ("where I had been").
 
• The phrase "all this while" is also adjusted to "all that while" to reflect the change in perspective.

Correct sentence: *He asked me where I had been all that while.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for converting direct to indirect speech:**
 
 
• If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the reported speech is shifted one step back in time (e.g., present perfect → past perfect).
 
• Pronouns and time expressions are adjusted to match the perspective of the speaker.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Direct: She said, "I am reading a book." → Indirect: She said that she was reading a book.
 
• Direct: He said, "I have finished my homework." → Indirect: He said that he had finished his homework.
